newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia allocates new farm machinery credits-paper.
newsitem.headline: Serbia allocates new farm machinery credits-paper.

text.p: Serbia's Development Fund has extended 100 million marks in new credits to metal-processing and machine-building industries for production of agricultural machinery, Belgrade daily Blic said on Tuesday.
Three-month credits were granted to 29 firms as a part of the government programme to revive production in the metal complex and deliver machinery and equipment to farm producers.

According to the plan, adopted in April, farm machinery will be exchanged for 16 agricultural products via contracts between Serbia's Commodity Reserve Agency and around 200 licenced companies throughout Serbia.
Machine producers should deliver to the Commodity Reserves 4,662 tractors, 270 combines, 280 maize harvesters and other machinery and equipment under the second part of the programme.

The government has already implemented a similar scheme with 20 local manufacturers, obliging them to deliver 2,200 tractors, 150 grain combines, 220 maize harvesters, 400 wheat sowers and 50 various kinds of machines and auxiliary equipment by the end of July 1997. No details were available on whether Programme 1 was fulfilled.
Serbia is estimated to have 418,000 tractors, 250,000 multi-cultivators and 24,000 combines and harvesters.

Serbia's Development Fund, the sole recipient of 80 percent of almost $1 billion raised from the sale of a 49 percent stake in Telekom Srbija to Italian and Greek partners early in June, has already disbursed around 500 million marks of credits to support its ailing industries and farm sector.
The government promised funds would be used to finance export industries, infrastructure and other development projects. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 311 4305
